newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac keeps China visit despite French election.
newsitem.headline: Chirac keeps China visit despite French election.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac told a senior Chinese official on Tuesday that he would honour a pledge to visit China despite a snap parliamentary election "because it was very important to him", a Chirac aide said.

Chinese Vice-Premier Zou Jiahua responded that Beijing was carefully preparing for Chirac's visit because it believed it would strengthen China's ties with France and Europe and bolster global peace and stability, Chirac spokeswoman Catherine Colonna told reporters.
The visit is due to take place on May 15-18.

Chirac agreed his trip should strengthen ties between China, France and Europe, Colonna said, adding that the two men's talks at the Elysee presidential palace took place in "a friendly working atmosphere".

Chirac aides first disclosed two weeks ago that Chirac would honour plans to visit China even though the trip fell just before France's May 25-June 1 snap parliamentary election, called by Chirac 10 months early and after the China trip had been scheduled.
Chirac told Zou that Europe was the world's top economic power and said China owed its rapid growth and development "to its policies of openness and modernisation", Colonna said.
"For these reasons, we must work for closer relations between Europe and Asia, Europe and China, by improving political as well as cultural and economic ties," she quoted Chirac as saying.

France's opposition Socialists have accused the governing centre-right of playing down differences with China over its human rights record in order to strengthen economic ties with Beijing and win new contracts for French businesses.

Political foes say announcements of new business deals in Beijing will strengthen Chirac's hand in the election campaign, where opinion polls show the left within striking distance of turning the centre-right out of power.
Chirac plans to visit Beijing and Shanghai, where a French trade exhibition will be open, but he dropped a planned stopover in Hong Kong due to the election campaign, aides had announced earlier.
Accompanied by his wife Bernadette and several senior ministers, he is expected to make strong overtures in favour of French industries, including arms manufacturers, the aides said.
Chinese Prime Minister Li Peng visited France last year and parliament head Qiao Shi met Chirac in Paris on March 27.
